# zdrot

> Applies a plane rotation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zdrot from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zdrot';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zdrot( N, x, strideX, y, strideY, c, s ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `zx` stride length |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `zy` stride length |
| `c` | `number` | Cosine of rotation (real) |
| `s` | `number` | Sine of rotation (real) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: On entry, N specifies the order of the vectors cx and cy. N must be at least zero.
- `x`: ( 1 + ( N - 1 )\*abs( `INCX` ) ). Before entry, the incremented array `ZX` must contain the n element vector cx. On exit, `ZX` is overwritten by the updated vector cx.
- `y`: ( 1 + ( N - 1 )\*abs( `INCY` ) ). Before entry, the incremented array `ZY` must contain the n element vector cy. On exit, `ZY` is overwritten by the updated vector cy.
- `c`: On entry, C specifies the cosine, cos.
- `s`: On entry, S specifies the sine, sin.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: output array

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zdrot.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY, c, s ) → Complex128Array
```

Applies a plane rotation, using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · First complex input/output vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride for `zx` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `zx` (in complex elements) |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Second complex input/output vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride for `zy` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `zy` (in complex elements) |
| `c` | `number` | Cosine of rotation (real) |
| `s` | `number` | Sine of rotation (real) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: On entry, N specifies the order of the vectors cx and cy. N must be at least zero.
- `x`: ( 1 + ( N - 1 )\*abs( `INCX` ) ). Before entry, the incremented array `ZX` must contain the n element vector cx. On exit, `ZX` is overwritten by the updated vector cx.
- `y`: ( 1 + ( N - 1 )\*abs( `INCY` ) ). Before entry, the incremented array `ZY` must contain the n element vector cy. On exit, `ZY` is overwritten by the updated vector cy.
- `c`: On entry, C specifies the cosine, cos.
- `s`: On entry, S specifies the sine, sin.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `zx`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zdrot()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`ZDROT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/zdrot.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zdrot from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zdrot';

// Apply a real Givens rotation to complex vectors:
const zx = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
const zy = new Complex128Array( [ 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
zdrot( 2, zx, 1, zy, 1, 0.8, 0.6 );
console.log( reinterpret( zx, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( reinterpret( zy, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
zdrot.ndarray( 2, zx, 1, 0, zy, 1, 0, 0.8, 0.6 );
console.log( reinterpret( zx, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( reinterpret( zy, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `ZDROT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

Applies a plane rotation, where the cos and sin (c and s) are real and the vectors cx and cy are complex. jack dongarra, linpack, 3/11/78.

</section>
